notes: 17 cases: 11 positive (should_trigger true) / 6 negative (should_trigger false). By origin: 5 golden (authored), 6 real-trace (byte-verbatim production user turns), 6 negative (authored near-misses). Real-trace provenance, one case per file, all six re-confirmed byte-verbatim on 2026-07-28 (method and the blockquote-prefix gotcha: verification_log.real_trace_verbatim): real-trace-01 docs/conversations/session-2026-06-03-2b8fda15.md; real-trace-02 session-2026-05-24-ac37bb09.md; real-trace-03 session-2026-06-15-156c224e.md; real-trace-04 session-2026-05-22-bbfc293b.md; real-trace-05 session-2026-05-29-ad634bc4.md; real-trace-06 session-2026-05-18-b0e6a559.md. Real-trace prompts are reproduced byte-for-byte INCLUDING curly apostrophes (U+2019 in real-trace-03) and lowercase/typo'd spelling; do not straighten or tidy them. EVERY case is designed to be satisfiable in the runner's clean temp workspace (a fresh mkdtemp cwd containing only .claude/skills/checkit; no git, no branch, no open PRs, no knowledge graph, no repo files) — see each case's workspace_requires. connects_to_active_work survives on exactly one case (golden-01), whose prompt supplies the active-work context inline. EVERY negative carries assertions that can fail; none has an empty expected_checks list. no_clarifying_question_bounced_back is asserted on ALL 11 positives; it is the skill's one rule, so no positive is allowed to pass while handing articulation back to the user. Authored prompts are written in the same register as the production traces (lowercase, comma splices, dropped apostrophes, no em dashes). A polished em-dash-heavy prompt is out-of-distribution for this user's actual turns and would measure routing on a text style the skill never sees in production; none of the six real traces contains an em dash.

execution_contract.advisory: Documentation only — runner.py does not read this object; it is here so the intended contract is reviewable and so a drift between intent and CLI flags is visible. Values mirror runner.py's module constants at authoring time.
execution_contract.workspace: clean temp dir per trial; skill installed at .claude/skills/checkit; --setting-sources project; --permission-mode bypassPermissions; --no-session-persistence
execution_contract.negative_semantics: runner.grade_trial scores a should_trigger:false trial FAIL the moment transcript.triggered(skill) is true, BEFORE expected_checks are consulted. The checks listed on a negative are therefore additive assertions about what the agent did INSTEAD of firing — they do not replace the non-trigger assertion, they stop the case from resting on it alone.

verification_log.advisory: Documentation only — runner.py does not read this object. A dated record of the LITERAL statuses observed, so a later reviewer can tell a stale claim from a re-checked one instead of trusting the prose in each case's 'verified' field.
verification_log.method: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' with a browser UA and a 25s cap, plus a separate HEAD for the Location header; JSON payloads parsed with python3, not eyeballed.

open_finding_against_the_skill.advisory: Documentation only. Raised by round-2 review, adjudicated here against both source documents; the fix belongs to the SKILL, not to this eval set.
open_finding_against_the_skill.finding: The skill's two documents disagree about whether a fully-specified artifact ask is in scope. references/checkit-lens.md:42-43 states branch 1 as 'Artifact present (URL / repo / paper / file / @-mention / image / pasted doc) -> run the full ingest pipeline using the taxonomy below', with NO under-specification condition, and its branch 3 guard at :46-48 excludes only 'a stray pointer phrase with no artifact and no topic, or an off-topic match'. Read literally, that gate routes ANY present artifact into the pipeline. SKILL.md:176 and the frontmatter description's NOT-FOR clause both explicitly carve the case out ('fully-specified artifact asks (answer directly)'). The lens's own preamble is about under-specified pointers throughout, so the disagreement looks like an omission in the branch-1 wording rather than a deliberate difference, but as written the two documents give opposite verdicts on negative-01, negative-03, and negative-06.
open_finding_against_the_skill.adjudication: Those three cases stay should_trigger:false, labelled by the DESCRIPTION, because the frontmatter description is what actually drives triggering — the lens is a reference the skill loads after it has already fired. No eval-side change follows from this finding.
open_finding_against_the_skill.suggested_skill_fix: One line in checkit-lens.md:42-43 — make branch 1 read 'Artifact present AND the ask is under-specified -> run the full ingest pipeline', and extend the branch-3 guard at :46-48 to name the fully-specified artifact ask as the other non-checkit shape. That makes the gate agree with SKILL.md:176 and the description.

known_gaps.no_bare_image_case: The harness passes each prompt as a text argument (LiveRunner.build_argv -> `-p <prompt>`), so there is no seam for attaching image bytes. A genuine bare-image artifact case is therefore not expressible today and is deliberately omitted rather than faked with an image URL, which would test URL fetching, not image ingestion.
known_gaps.no_production_sourced_negative: docs/conversations/ was searched for a real user turn that is a single-axis near-miss (artifact present + ask fully specified). None was found: production turns in this workspace that carry an artifact are almost uniformly under-specified, which is why the skill exists. All six negatives are therefore authored. This is stated rather than papered over with a synthesised 'real trace'.
known_gaps.no_askless_conversational_negative: The set has no negative in which a trigger phrase is used with NO ask at all — 'check this out, <status update>, felt good.' negative-05 was that case for one revision and was changed away from it deliberately, not by oversight. Reason: the correct response to an ask-less status update is a short conversational acknowledgement, and every additive check this registry offers penalises short correct answers. THE REASON IS STILL TRUE BUT THE MECHANISM STATED HERE IS NOT — corrected 2026-07-28, having been written against two thresholds that no longer exist. It is NOT 'final_answer_non_empty needs >=40 chars' (it counts words, floor 3) and NOT 'no_clarifying_question_bounced_back fails any sub-400-char answer ending in ?' (length was removed as a discriminator entirely; a trailing OFFER now passes, and only a question that hands articulation back fails). What actually still bites, re-measured against the current checks: an acknowledgement leaves almost no ANSWER behind once its trailing question is peeled, so 'Big one. Want me to write that up?' (2 words of body) and 'Nice. Want me to note it?' (1 word) both still fail — the whole-turn arm, not a length rule. Such a case can therefore still only rest on the runner's non-trigger assertion alone, which is exactly what every negative here is required not to do. Reopen this gap when the registry gains an absence-of-over-delivery check (see checks_the_registry_lacks), which would let an ask-less negative assert something real.
known_gaps.checks_the_registry_lacks: Three assertions a negative would ideally make have no CHECK_REGISTRY entry and are NOT referenced here (an unknown id is a hard PromptSetError, which would make the whole set unloadable): (1) skill_not_triggered — an explicit positive-form assertion that the skill stayed quiet, so the non-trigger claim appears in expected_checks instead of only in grade_trial's control flow; (2) no_unrequested_documentation — asserts the agent did NOT file notes/entities on a fully-specified ask (the over-delivery failure mode of negative-01/03/06); (3) no_unrequested_next_steps — asserts the agent did NOT append a ranked next-steps list to a bounded answer. Until those exist the negatives assert non-trigger (via the runner) plus answer-quality, not absence-of-over-delivery.

checks_withdrawn_2026_07_28.why: Withdrawn from every case after four adversarial P20 rounds in which each fix oscillated between false-passing and false-failing. A check that rejects correct behaviour is worse than no check: it depresses a CORRECT agent's measured pass rate, so a real regression hides among the false-fails, and the rational response is to lower the threshold. See research/entities/pattern/anti-vacuity-fixes-overshoot-into-noise.md.
checks_withdrawn_2026_07_28.no_clarifying_question_bounced_back: Was asserted on 17/17 cases. Round 3: a bare prefix match with no interrogative requirement — 7/7 declarative answers containing zero questions scored as clarifying questions ('Which one wins depends on how often you bump the lockfile.'). Round 4 fixed that and regressed elsewhere: any wh-question containing you/your scored a bounce even when the agent answered it in the next clause, and 'What if I run it with the lock disabled?' — the same speech act as the accepted 'How about I benchmark it?' — scored 'demanding content'. 5 of 18 plausible correct replies to this file's OWN negatives failed, across 5 of 6 negatives. The distinction it encodes (bounce = asks the user to specify the ask; offer = states a result then proposes a declinable step) is a semantic judgement. A regex is the wrong instrument; this belongs behind the LLM-judge seam.
checks_withdrawn_2026_07_28.ingests_full_artifact_not_metadata: Withdrawn because it now FAILS OPEN. _is_path_shaped drops one-slash extensionless references, so 'gepa-ai/gepa' yields an EMPTY token set and _hits_artifact returns True unconditionally — proven: Read{'/etc/hosts'} PASSES. The round-3 form failed the other way (host-level scoping: fetching a DIFFERENT github repo or arXiv paper PASSED). Correct scoping has to survive redirect indirection (golden-04's substance sits behind a t.co at x.com/i/article/...), which token matching does not model.
checks_withdrawn_2026_07_28.what_still_holds: Negatives are NOT weakened by this withdrawal: a negative's PRIMARY assertion is structural, not regex — runner.py:1046-1048 fails any negative where the skill triggered ('over-triggered on a near-miss prompt'). expected_checks were always supplementary. v1 therefore grades TRIGGERING deterministically, which is the failure mode the arc measured (Schmid: ~50% of skill failures are trigger failures). Outcome grading beyond the surviving checks needs the LLM-judge seam and is tracked separately.
checks_withdrawn_2026_07_28.note_on_no_permission_denials: Retained but weak by construction: the runner launches with --permission-mode bypassPermissions, so it cannot fail on agent behaviour, only on a sandbox anomaly. Kept as a run-health sentinel.

cases.prompt:
here's the whole thing, tell me what you make of it.

## Expiry-aware lease (draft)

A lease is one row: (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, holder TEXT, expires_at INTEGER).

acquire(key, holder, ttl) — one statement, no transaction:

    INSERT INTO lease (key, holder, expires_at)
    VALUES (?, ?, :now + :ttl)
    ON CONFLICT(key) DO UPDATE
      SET holder = excluded.holder, expires_at = excluded.expires_at
      WHERE lease.expires_at <= :now
    RETURNING holder;

The caller holds the lease iff the returned holder is its own. A live lease held
by someone else returns their holder, not an error.

renew(key, holder, ttl) — same shape with WHERE lease.holder = ?.
release(key, holder) — DELETE WHERE key = ? AND holder = ?.

Open: clock skew across processes writing :now; whether renew extends from now or
from the old expires_at; what happens to work already in flight when a lease
lapses mid-run.

cases.verified: n/a — no external source. Replaces the previous docs/inbox/keel-spec.md, which does not exist anywhere in the repo (find -name keel-spec.md returned nothing) and could never have been read from a clean temp workspace.
cases.workspace_requires: none — the artifact IS the prompt. No filesystem path, no network. This is the case that proves an under-specified artifact ask is gradeable with zero environmental dependencies.
cases.rationale: Pasted-document artifact with an under-specified directive: 'tell me what you make of it' names no output contract, no depth, no format. The spec carries a real mechanism (a conditional-upsert compare-and-swap) and three stated open questions, so traverses_to_primitives and produces_ranked_next_steps are earned by engaging with the design rather than restating it. mentions_source_verification and ingests_full_artifact_not_metadata are deliberately absent: there is no external source to verify and no fetch to perform, so asserting them would grade the environment, not the run. Register note: the user's own line carries no em dash, matching the production traces; the em dashes inside the pasted body are intentional, because a pasted design doc is written in a different register from the chat turn that carries it.

cases.artifact: social post — X status by @0xCodez whose own body is empty; it carries an X Article (long-form, 16 embedded images)
cases.verified: REAL, re-verified 2026-07-28. api.fxtwitter.com/0xCodez/status/2079165300625330317 returns code 200 with author screen_name 0xCodez; control status id 1111111111111111111 returns code 404. CORRECTION OF A PRIOR OVER-CLAIM: an earlier revision of THIS field asserted 'the payload is media'. That was an inference, not an observation, and it is false — tweet.media is null and the media key list is empty. What the payload actually contains, read off the response: tweet.text is the EMPTY string; tweet.raw_text.text is the bare link https://t.co/WVztfCUH4u; that t.co returns 301 -> https://x.com/i/article/2079141496981184512, an X ARTICLE (article.id 2079141496981184512, title 'Graph Engineering with Claude: 14-Step roadmap from 0 to graph architect (Full Course)', created 2026-07-20; content.blocks = 151 blocks / ~15.7k chars of prose, of which 40 are atomic blocks; cover_media plus 16 media_entities, every one of __typename ApiImage; sampled body image https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HNqn3q8XoAAXCdJ.jpg returns 200). Separately observed and kept deliberately: the prompt's own URL returns 307 -> /0xCodez/status/2079165300625330317, which is X normalising the handle's case. That is unlike golden-05's redirect, which followed a repo RENAME and could silently retarget the artifact; a case-fold cannot, so the lowercase form a user would actually paste is left in the prompt.
cases.artifact_aliases_note: Documentation for the field above; runner.py reads only 'artifact_aliases'. This is the ONE case in the set whose substance sits behind an indirection: the status body is the empty string and its raw_text is the bare t.co link, which 301s to the X Article (both hops recorded in verification_log.url_status). Artifact scoping is token-based, and the article URL shares with the prompt only the host 'x.com' — a token checks._is_distinctive rightly refuses, because scoping on it would pass ANY x.com fetch, including a different user's post. Without these aliases the CORRECT route (follow the redirect, read the article) scores FAIL on ingests_full_artifact_not_metadata while a wrong-artifact fetch of some other x.com status scores PASS, which is the scoping backwards. The field is additive only: it adds the tokens '2079141496981184512' and 'wvztfcuh4u', and cannot make a fetch of a different artifact pass.
cases.rationale: Social-post artifact plus a one-word directive; 'thoughts?' is a paraphrase of wdyt, not a verbatim USE WHEN entry. BRANCH CLAIM CORRECTED to match the payload actually observed above. This is the taxonomy's 'Blog post / article / thread' row (references/checkit-lens.md:57), NOT a media post. It remains the sharpest ingests_full_artifact_not_metadata case in the set, and for a stronger reason than the one previously claimed: the status renders as NOTHING — text is the empty string, raw_text is a bare t.co link — so every word of substance sits behind one indirection into the linked article. An agent that stops at the status has literally zero content to report on, which is precisely the metadata-only failure that check exists to catch. The 'text is only half the artifact, pull the pixels too' clause (SKILL.md:109-116) does apply here, again for the corrected reason: the substance is a 15.7k-char article carrying a cover image plus 16 embedded images, so a text-only extractor drops the pixels. On the mentions_source_verification objection: SKILL.md:112 records that WebFetch 402s on x.com, so a run may legitimately fail to read the post. That does NOT make the check self-contradictory here — checks._VERIFY_RE matches 'could not confirm', 'could not verify', and 'unverified', so an honest report that the source could not be reached SATISFIES the check. What fails it is silence about provenance: an answer that asserts what the post says without ever addressing whether the source was actually reached.

A real artifact, research-adjacent vocabulary, and a genuine fetch-and-extract job — but the columns, the format, and the stopping condition ('table only') are all stated, so there is nothing left to infer. Deliberately NOT the description's own example string: the previous version of this case was 'summarize this PDF in 3 bullets', copied verbatim out of the NOT-FOR clause, which tested whether a model can read an exclusion list pasted into its own context. cases.workspace_requires: none. Rewritten from the previous version, which named 'the gate slice' and 'the P20 round' with no context: in a clean temp workspace that prompt was unanswerable, so a clarifying question would have been the CORRECT response and the case would have punished it. Every fact needed to decide is now supplied inline.
cases.rationale: Near-miss on the strongest trigger word. CORRECTED RATIONALE: the previous version claimed the gate 'requires a shared URL/repo/paper/file/image/doc', which contradicts the skill's own spec — references/checkit-lens.md:44-45 defines branch 2, 'No artifact, but a research-topic -> run the same pipeline with the topic as the subject', and SKILL.md:174-175 lists 'a bare topic string' as in scope.
